title: add-rag-concurrency-profiles-and-workload-harness-examples
author: Maya Patel
description: Add a small, focused RAG concurrency/workload harness and a set of example agents that demonstrate adaptive batching and concurrency profiles for different deployment modes. Motivation: teams frequently ask how to translate token throughput targets into concurrent request limits and batching settings; this PR provides a reproducible harness, sample workload profiles (low-latency, cost-optimized, bursty-batch), and annotated agent examples that show tool-calling when KV-cache hits occur. Changes include: a lightweight workload generator (TS) that can replay recorded prompt traces with configurable qps and token distributions; three concurrency profile manifests (hosted-realtime, dedicated-throughput, edge-burst) with recommended default settings and rationale; two agent samples (agent-adaptive-batcher.ts, agent-prefetch-indexer.ts) demonstrating token-aware prefetching and prefix caching; a small docs quickstart (docs/quickstarts/rag-concurrency.md) that walks through running the harness locally, interpreting latency vs cost tradeoffs, tuning autoscale thresholds for Redwood Dedicated, and a suggested smoke test to add to CI. The description includes usage examples for the local harness CLI (one-line): yarn harness --profile hosted-realtime --qps 10 --duration 300 --out ./artifacts. The PR also wires the harness into the examples CI smoke matrix and adds unit tests for the batching decision module. Related: ENG-1452 (throughput profiler) and SUP-884 (support ticket about unexplained tail latency with small sequences). Checklist: [x] add harness and profiles, [x] add agent examples, [x] add docs quickstart and examples README, [x] CI smoke, [x] unit tests for batching heuristics. Links: Linear ENG-1452 https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1452, Support SUP-884 (internal).

release_notes: Add RAG concurrency harness and examples for adaptive batching. Exposes recommended profiles for hosted, dedicated, and edge deployments; includes quickstart docs and CI smoke integration. Useful for teams tuning latency vs cost tradeoffs.
notes_for_operators: Profiles are intentionally conservative; dedicated-throughput uses larger batch windows and higher max concurrency. See docs/quickstarts/rag-concurrency.md for tuning guidance. For Private installs, ensure KMS-access for artifact export when running the harness in gated environments.
